title: Bombay High Court Convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 Rape Case, Sentences Him to 10 Years
excerpt: The Bombay High Court overturned the Tehelka founder's 2021 acquittal, convicting him of raping a colleague during a conference in Goa and sentencing him to a decade of rigorous imprisonment.
body:
• Bombay High Court convicted former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal of rape and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment, overturning his 2021 acquittal.
  • The case stems from the alleged sexual assault of a female colleague during a conference in Goa in November 2013, making it one of India's longest-running high-profile sexual assault trials.
  • Tejpal has maintained his innocence and said he will appeal the verdict in the Supreme Court, calling himself a political victim.

A two-judge bench of the Bombay High Court on Wednesday convicted former journalist and Tehelka magazine founder Tarun Tejpal of raping a colleague 12 years ago, sentencing him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment in a case that had become a lightning rod for debates about the safety of women in Indian workplaces.

The Goa bench of the high court set aside a 2021 acquittal by a lower trial court in the coastal state, where the crime took place during the magazine's THiNK festival in November 2013. Tejpal, 62, was accused by a female colleague of sexually assaulting and raping her inside a hotel elevator at a five-star resort over two successive nights.

A Landmark Reversal

The conviction marks a dramatic reversal in a case that has wound through India's courts for over a decade. In May 2021, a sessions court in Mapusa had acquitted Tejpal of all charges, with the trial judge drawing criticism for observations about the complainant's behaviour and lifestyle rather than focusing on the accused's conduct.

The State of Goa challenged the acquittal before the Bombay High Court, with Solicitor General Tushar Mehta arguing on behalf of the prosecution that the trial court had effectively "put the complainant on trial." Mehta contended that the lower court relied on the woman's personal life, post-incident messages, and perceived normative behaviour to reach a verdict that amounted to "a classic case of perversity."

The high court heard arguments across seven sessions before a division bench of Justice Neela Gokhale and Justice Amit Borkar Jamsandekar before reserving judgment last week.

The Rise and Fall of Tehelka

Tejpal co-founded Tehelka in 2000 as India's first major online journalism platform. The publication gained national prominence through a series of sting operations, most notably Operation West End, which exposed corruption in defence procurement. At its peak, Tehelka was regarded as a pioneering force in Indian investigative journalism, winning multiple awards and earning Tejpal recognition from Business Week as one of Asia's top 50 leaders.

The sexual assault allegations in 2013 effectively ended both Tejpal's career and Tehelka's operations. The trial, which began only in September 2017 after years of procedural delays, became one of India's most closely watched cases on sexual violence in the workplace.

Defence and Next Steps

Tejpal has maintained his innocence throughout. His defence team, led by senior advocate Aabad Ponda, had argued that the acquittal was based on a comprehensive evaluation of evidence including CCTV footage, panchanama records, and expert testimony. Ponda contended that the prosecution had wrongly interpreted Tejpal's apology emails as admissions of physical assault, arguing they referred only to a "consensual verbal conversation of a sexual nature."

Following the conviction, Tejpal said he was a political victim and would challenge the verdict before the Supreme Court. The court has ordered him to surrender to authorities within four weeks, according to Goa's top government lawyer Devidas Pangam.

There was no comment from the complainant, who cannot be identified under Indian law to protect her privacy.

Wider Implications

The verdict arrives more than a decade after the incident and eight years after the MeToo movement swept through India in 2018, raising uncomfortable questions about accountability timelines in sexual assault cases involving powerful figures. The case underscores both the persistence of survivors seeking justice and the slow pace at which the Indian judicial system processes such cases.

For the Indian diaspora, which watched Tehelka's rise as a symbol of independent media's potential in India, the conviction marks a sobering chapter. Tejpal, once celebrated as a crusading editor who held power to account, now faces prison for abusing his own position of authority.
nri_angle: The conviction of Tejpal, whose Tehelka magazine shaped how the Indian diaspora understood investigative journalism back home, raises questions about accountability in India's media elite.
